title: Polyglot runbooks: LLM proxy & app example templates for Next.js, FastAPI, Go, and CLI
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a set of small, opinionated polyglot example projects and runbooks that demonstrate best practices for using Redwood SDKs and the Redwood API in real apps. Target languages/frameworks: Next.js (TypeScript), FastAPI (Python), Go HTTP server, and a cross-platform CLI (Go or Python). Each example should include: README, minimal Dockerfile, CI workflow, instrumentation snippets (Prometheus/Datadog), retry/backoff patterns, streaming ergonomics (server-side and client-side examples), graceful shutdown, token-cost telemetry hooks, and a short cookbook section with 3 bite-sized snippets (retries, streaming resume, and KV cache usage). The goal is low-friction sample apps that teams can copy into repos or use as integration tests for SDK releases.
acceptance_criteria: One Next.js template with client streaming example + API route proxy + docs on streaming ergonomics
One FastAPI example demonstrating async streaming, retry middleware, and Docker/uvicorn production notes
One idiomatic Go HTTP server showing streaming via ResponseWriter + example CLI invoking Redwood API with exponential backoff
A cross-platform CLI example with resume token example and metrics emission
Each repo contains CI (lint/test/build), Dockerfile, small e2e test that runs against a test Redwood API token, and a short cookbook.md with 3 copy-paste snippets
PRs merged and smoke-tested on staging; README includes cost/latency tradeoffs and recommended defaults
comments: 2026-02-21 - Discovery: Spent time cataloging gaps in existing example repo—most samples show single-sync call; none demonstrate streaming resume or graceful shutdown. Decided to target streaming resume and cost-safety patterns.

2026-02-25 - Design decision: Use native Fetch streaming in Next.js Edge runtime for demo, include alternative using SSE in pages/api for targets without Edge. Rationale: Fetch streaming is closer to production serverless edge deployment and simpler for client demos. (Reviewed by Alex Chen)

2026-02-27 - Trade-off note: For retries we debated using SDK built-in retry vs example middleware. Chose to implement a transparent middleware layer in examples that wraps SDK calls to surface backoff knobs; this avoids duplication when SDK retries are updated.

2026-03-01 - PoC complete for FastAPI streaming route + small test. Found Uvicorn's default timeout kills long-lived streams; added guidance in README to set --timeout-keep-alive and to use ASGI lifespan for graceful shutdown.
2026-03-03 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/456 — includes Next.js and FastAPI scaffolds; requesting review from @alex.chen and @lucy-ng.

2026-03-05 - Code review feedback from Alex Chen: add more granular metrics (per-route token count), and a note to avoid shipping real API keys in CI — added secrets example and ephemeral test tokens section.
2026-03-06 - Blocker: SDK streaming API changed (ENG-128204) — awaiting compatibility patch. Temporary workaround added in Go example to use low-level http client until patch lands.

2026-03-08 - Next steps: finish Go server example, add CLI resume token snippet, write cookbook.md and finalize PRs. Planning to run smoke tests against staging on 2026-03-15 before merge to main branch.
attachments: Figma (UX snippet flows for streaming UX): https://www.figma.com/file/abcdef/streaming-ux
notes: Implementation notes: keep examples slim (under 150 LOC per language) so they are easy to copy into customer repos.
Testing: include a small harness that can flip between real Redwood API and the local test server (env var REDWOOD_API_URL).
Docs: emphasize cost/latency tradeoffs — show token-counting hook and an example of prefix caching to reduce token spend.
Follow-ups: propose a separate doc for advanced batching/quantization recommendations after initial examples land.
Design constraints: examples must avoid experimental SDK APIs; if SDK changes are required, coordinate with SDK owners and add a compatibility shim in the examples repo.
